subject: music
title: Strings & Woodwind
welcome_lead: Bows on strings and breath through wood.
meta_desc: KS3 instrument families: strings and woodwind.
final_note: Strings and woodwind start the orchestra families.

concepts.def: Family using breath through a tube.

walkthroughs.body_html: The orchestra string family is violin, viola, cello, double bass — biggest to smallest in tone. Strings are bowed, plucked or struck.
Woodwind includes flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon. Many were once made of wood. Sound comes from blowing across or through a reed.
The clarinet has a single reed. The oboe and bassoon have double reeds. The flute has no reed — you blow across an edge.

mcqs.q: What three notes form a major triad in root position?
options: A long melody with no breaks.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
A long melody with no breaks.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: Any two phrases of similar style.
Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
A long melody with no breaks.
